correctness.rationale: Product diagonalization gives eigenvalues 2cos(pi*j/(n+1))±1. A cross-band collision would have cosines differing by 1; normalized cyclotomic traces of 2cos bound the difference by 1, with equality only when orders are 6 and 3. Thus j=(n+1)/3, k=2(n+1)/3 yield the unique two-dimensional energy-zero eigenspace. Its equal-corner-amplitude cancellation produces the normalized displayed phi; 1D other eigenspaces all have nonzero corner amplitude. The rank-one dissipative Hamiltonian has strictly decaying bright spectrum, including Jordan blocks, and stationary dark projection, giving site probabilities and mixed trace. Independent exact characteristic polynomial gcd and local spectral projectors on bounded n corroborate. This covers all integers n>=2 and all gamma>0; no assertion for Laplacian/weighted/sink elsewhere.
residual_risks: Finite spectral tests do not establish the infinite trace obstruction; that step is proved using Ramanujan sums.
No claim about Laplacian walks, arbitrary traps or mean absorption time.
